slurmpilot Architecture

Source: ARCHITECTURE.md

slurmpilot is a CRAN-grade R package that provides an end-to-end pilot-to-cluster autopilot and non-blocking Shiny compute engine for computationally intensive R workloads (Monte Carlo simulations, Bayesian MCMC, mixed-effects and dynamic structural equation modeling, and large-scale bootstraps).

1. High-Level Modular Design

The package is organized into four cohesive pillars connected by explicit, immutable S3 specification objects and an R6 scheduler backend interface:

  User workload (fun, args_list, packages, globals)
         │
         ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pillar 1: Micro-Pilot Auto-Profiler                      │
│   R/pilot.R, R/resources.R                               │
│   pilot_run() ──► slurmpilot_pilot                       │
│   estimate_resources() ──► slurmpilot_resources          │
└───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (chunk_size, --mem, --time, --array)
         ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐
         ▼                                     ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Pillar 2: HPC Env & Packager     │  │ Pillar 3: Pluggable Scheduler Backends  │
│   R/env_scan.R, R/apptainer.R,   │  │   R/backend_base.R  (SlurmBackend R6)   │
│   R/sbatch.R                     │  │   R/backend_mock.R  (MockSlurmBackend)  │
│   scan_project_env()             │  │   R/backend_ssh.R   (SlurmSshBackend)   │
│   build_apptainer_def()          │  │   R/job.R           (S3 lifecycle API)  │
│   render_sbatch_script()         │  └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
│   render_worker_script()         │                       │
└──────────────────────────────────┘                       ▼

Source File Map

File Responsibility
R/slurmpilot-package.R Package documentation, @importFrom declarations, global variable registrations
R/utils.R Internal helpers: SLURM time/memory parsers & formatters, array range compression, atomic file I/O, chunk partitioning, shell quoting

R/resources.R estimate_resources(), resource_spec(), as_slurm_flags(), chunk sizing & scaling math; print method
R/env_scan.R scan_project_env(), toolchain_registry() scanning renv.lock, DESCRIPTION, and scripts to detect compiled toolchains and Debian/Ubuntu apt dependencies
R/apptainer.R build_apptainer_def() generating reproducible Apptainer/Singularity .def recipes with pinned base images, toolchains, renv restore, %environment, and %test

R/backend_base.R Abstract R6 class SlurmBackend defining the scheduler contract and shared job staging helpers
R/backend_mock.R MockSlurmBackend: local parallel background-process SLURM simulator using callr::r_bg + ps, disk checkpoints, queue limits, simulated OOM/TIMEOUT/FAIL faults, surgical retry, cancellation, and log capture
R/backend_ssh.R SlurmSshBackend + pure command/parser functions (build_ssh_args, build_scp_args, parse_sbatch_output, parse_squeue_output, parse_sacct_output, build_scancel_command) with injectable command_runner for deterministic contract testing
R/job.R User-facing S3 constructors and lifecycle API (slurm_job_spec, slurm_submit, slurm_status, slurm_retry, slurm_cancel, slurm_logs, slurm_collect, slurm_wait, slurm_autopilot)
R/shiny_submit.R mod_hpc_submit_ui() & mod_hpc_submit_server(): non-blocking micro-pilot + cluster submission module
R/shiny_monitor.R mod_hpc_monitor_ui() & mod_hpc_monitor_server(): live bslib telemetry dashboard with chunk progress bar, resource gauges, surgical retry, cancel, pause/resume, and log viewer
R/shiny_app.R run_demo_app() launcher for the bundled Monte Carlo simulation demo under inst/shiny/demo/app.R

2. Micro-Pilot Profiling & Resource Scaling Mathematics

2.1 Empirical Measurement Protocol

Naive profiling inside the main R session via system.time() and gc() systematically underestimates true cluster resource demand because: 1. gc() only sees R’s managed heap, missing C++/Stan/TMB/BLAS/OpenMP native allocations and shared libraries. 2. In-process timing omits cold R startup and package-loading overhead incurred by every SLURM array task.

pilot_run() solves both by launching each pilot trial i∈{1,…,npilot}i \in \{1, \dots, n_{\text{pilot}}\} inside an isolated background child R process via callr::r_bg() and polling the OS process tree (ps::ps_memory_info() summed across the worker PID and recursive children) at sample_interval seconds (default 0.05s).

Each child emits high-resolution internal checkpoints: - tspawnt_{\text{spawn}}: parent launches child process. - treadyt_{\text{ready}}: child R starts, loads requested packages, and reads the serialized payload. - tstart,tendt_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}: task function invocation boundaries.

From these checkpoints and OS samples we obtain per trial ii: - Startup overhead: t0,i=tready,i−tspawn,it_{0,i} = t_{\text{ready},i} - t_{\text{spawn},i} - Task execution time: t1,i=tend,i−tstart,it_{1,i} = t_{\text{end},i} - t_{\text{start},i} - Baseline RSS (m0,im_{0,i}): RSS sampled at worker readiness (R runtime + loaded packages). - Peak RSS (mpeak,im_{\text{peak},i}): Maximum total RSS observed across the worker process tree during trial ii. - Net working-set RSS (mnet,im_{\text{net},i}): max⁡(0,mpeak,i−m0,i)\max(0,\; m_{\text{peak},i} - m_{0,i}).

2.2 Scaling Model & Optimal Chunking (estimate_resources())

Given NN total tasks (n_tasks) and successful pilot measurements:

  1. Startup & Per-Task Time Parameters:

    • t̂0=median(t0,i)\hat{t}_0 = \text{median}(t_{0,i}) (fixed per-chunk startup cost).
    • μ̂t=mean(t1,i)\hat{\mu}_t = \text{mean}(t_{1,i}) (expected per-task execution time).
    • σ̂t=sd(t1,i)\hat{\sigma}_t = \text{sd}(t_{1,i}) (if nok<2n_{\text{ok}} < 2 or σ̂t=0\hat{\sigma}_t = 0, fallback to 0.25μ̂t0.25\,\hat{\mu}_t to preserve a nonzero uncertainty buffer).
    • q̂90\hat{q}_{90}: empirical 90th percentile of t1,it_{1,i}.

  2. CPU Scaling (Amdahl’s Law): If the pilot ran with c0c_0 CPUs and the target requests cc CPUs with parallel efficiency η∈(0,1]\eta \in (0, 1], the relative speedup factor is: S(c0→c)=(1−η)+η/c0(1−η)+η/cS(c_0 \to c) = \frac{(1 - \eta) + \eta / c_0}{(1 - \eta) + \eta / c} Notice S(c0→c0)=1S(c_0 \to c_0) = 1 identically, and effective per-task time parameters scale as μ̃t=μ̂t/S\tilde{\mu}_t = \hat{\mu}_t / S, σ̃t=σ̂t/S\tilde{\sigma}_t = \hat{\sigma}_t / S, q̃90=q̂90/S\tilde{q}_{90} = \hat{q}_{90} / S.

  3. Optimal Array Chunk Size (k*k^*): Let Ttarget=60⋅target_chunk_minutesT_{\text{target}} = 60 \cdot \text{target\_chunk\_minutes} be the target walltime per SLURM array task (default 15 minutes).

    • Time-targeted chunk size: ktime=max⁡(1,⌊max⁡(1,Ttarget−t̂0)max⁡(μ̃t,10−3)⌋)k_{\text{time}} = \max\!\left(1,\; \left\lfloor \frac{\max(1,\; T_{\text{target}} - \hat{t}_0)}{\max(\tilde{\mu}_t,\; 10^{-3})} \right\rfloor\right)
    • Array-limit lower bound (respecting SLURM MaxArraySize, default 1000): kcap=⌈Nmax_array_size⌉k_{\text{cap}} = \left\lceil \frac{N}{\text{max\_array\_size}} \right\rceil
    • Chosen chunk size: k*=clamp(max(ktime,kcap),kmin,min(N,kmax))k^* = \text{clamp}\!\left(\max(k_{\text{time}}, k_{\text{cap}}),\; k_{\min},\; \min(N, k_{\max})\right)
    • Number of SLURM array tasks: M=⌈Nk*⌉M = \left\lceil \frac{N}{k^*} \right\rceil
    • Amortized startup overhead ratio: ρoverhead=t̂0t̂0+k*μ̃t\rho_{\text{overhead}} = \frac{\hat{t}_0}{\hat{t}_0 + k^* \tilde{\mu}_t}

  4. Conservative Walltime Limit (--time): Across k*k^* independent sequential replications inside one chunk, the sum’s standard deviation grows as k*σ̃t\sqrt{k^*}\,\tilde{\sigma}_t. Using small-sample tt-quantile ztail=t0.99,df=max⁡(1,nok−1)z_{\text{tail}} = t_{0.99,\; \text{df} = \max(1, n_{\text{ok}} - 1)} capped at 3.53.5 (and floored at 2.3262.326 for large nn): Tpred(k*)=max⁡(t̂0+k*μ̃t+ztailk*σ̃t,t̂0+k*q̃90)T_{\text{pred}}(k^*) = \max\!\left(\hat{t}_0 + k^*\tilde{\mu}_t + z_{\text{tail}}\sqrt{k^*}\,\tilde{\sigma}_t,\; \hat{t}_0 + k^*\tilde{q}_{90}\right)Treq=ceil_to(max(Tmin,γtime⋅Tpred(k*)),ΔT)T_{\text{req}} = \text{ceil\_to}\!\left(\max\!\left(T_{\min},\; \gamma_{\text{time}} \cdot T_{\text{pred}}(k^*)\right),\; \Delta_T\right) where γtime=time_safety\gamma_{\text{time}} = \text{time\_safety} (default 1.50) and ΔT=time_round_minutes\Delta_T = \text{time\_round\_minutes} (default 5 minutes).

  5. Conservative Memory Limit (--mem): Sequential tasks reuse the R heap, but long-running chunks exhibit modest memory fragmentation modeled logarithmically in k*k^*: Mbase=max⁡(maximpeak,i,median(m0,i)+maximnet,i)M_{\text{base}} = \max\!\left(\max_i m_{\text{peak},i},\; \text{median}(m_{0,i}) + \max_i m_{\text{net},i}\right)Mpred=Mbase⋅(1+0.05log⁡2(max(1,k*)))⋅(1+0.15⋅max(0,c−c0))M_{\text{pred}} = M_{\text{base}} \cdot \left(1 + 0.05 \log_2(\max(1, k^*))\right) \cdot \left(1 + 0.15 \cdot \max(0, c - c_0)\right)Mreq=ceil_to(max(Mmin,γmem⋅Mpred),ΔM)M_{\text{req}} = \text{ceil\_to}\!\left(\max\!\left(M_{\min},\; \gamma_{\text{mem}} \cdot M_{\text{pred}}\right),\; \Delta_M\right) where γmem=mem_safety\gamma_{\text{mem}} = \text{mem\_safety} (default 1.35), Mmin=512 MBM_{\min} = 512\text{ MB}, and ΔM=256 MB\Delta_M = 256\text{ MB}.

3. HPC Environment, Apptainer & SLURM Contract

3.1 Toolchain & Dependency Scanning (scan_project_env())

Scans three complementary sources in a project directory: 1. renv.lock (JSON) — pins R version, package versions, and repositories. 2. DESCRIPTION (DCF) — extracts Depends, Imports, and optionally Suggests. 3. Project .R, .Rmd, and .qmd source files — parses library(), require(), requireNamespace(), and pkg::fn references.

Detected packages are matched against toolchain_registry() to infer compiled toolchains (cpp, cmdstan, rstan, tmb, jags, spatial, http_ssl, linear_algebra, graphics, arrow) and the exact minimal Debian/Ubuntu apt-get system packages required inside a rocker/r-ver:<R_version> container.

3.2 Apptainer .def Contract (build_apptainer_def())

Produces deterministic, reproducible Apptainer/Singularity definition files: - Bootstrap: docker / From: rocker/r-ver:<r_version> - %labels: provenance tags (GeneratedBy slurmpilot, RVersion, Toolchains, deterministic EnvHash) - %files: copies renv.lock when renv_restore = TRUE - %environment: pins UTF-8 locale, single-threaded BLAS/OpenMP defaults (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1) to prevent oversubscription across SLURM array jobs, and CMDSTAN=/opt/cmdstan when cmdstanr is active - %post: non-interactive apt-get install --no-install-recommends, ~/.R/Makevars optimization flags for compiled toolchains, renv::restore() (or explicit install.packages() from Posit Package Manager binaries), optional CmdStan build, and apt cache cleanup - %test: smoke-tests package loading and CmdStan availability during apptainer build - %runscript: exec Rscript "$@"

3.3 Job Staging Directory & Standalone Worker Contract

Every job submitted by either MockSlurmBackend or SlurmSshBackend uses the exact same deterministic workspace layout:

<job_dir>/
├── payload.rds            # Serialized list: fun, args_list, packages, globals, seed
├── chunks.json            # Array index -> task index mapping & resource spec
├── worker.R               # Standalone base-R runner (requires ZERO slurmpilot install on HPC!)
├── submit.sbatch          # Primary SLURM array submission script
├── retry_<k>.sbatch       # Surgical retry script for failed array indices only
├── state.json             # Job metadata, backend job IDs, attempt history
├── status/
│   └── chunk_<id>.json    # Per-chunk machine-readable telemetry & terminal state
├── results/
│   └── chunk_<id>.rds     # Atomic checkpoint of task outputs for chunk <id>
└── logs/
    ├── chunk_<id>.out     # Stdout log
    └── chunk_<id>.err     # Stderr log

Atomic Checkpointing Rule: worker.R writes each chunk’s result to results/.chunk_<id>.rds.tmp.<pid> and atomically renames it to results/chunk_<id>.rds via file.rename(). Therefore, a mid-write OOM kill or node preemption can never leave a half-written corrupt .rds artifact. On surgical retry, completed chunks with valid results/chunk_<id>.rds are untouched and never re-executed.

4. Pluggable Scheduler Backend Interface

4.1 SlurmBackend R6 Abstract Contract

All scheduler implementations inherit from SlurmBackend and implement: - submit(job_spec) → slurmpilot_job - status(job) → slurmpilot_status - retry(job, chunks = NULL, resources = NULL) → updated slurmpilot_job - cancel(job, chunks = NULL) → slurmpilot_status (invisibly) - logs(job, chunk_id = NULL) → named character vector / list of stdout & stderr logs - collect(job, simplify = FALSE, allow_partial = FALSE) → ordered list (or simplified vector/tibble) of task results - wait(job, timeout = Inf, poll_interval = 0.25, progress = FALSE) → terminal slurmpilot_status

4.2 Chunk State Machine

                submit() / retry()
  [NEW] ───────────────────────────────► PENDING
                                            │ slot available
                                            ▼
                                         RUNNING ──► cancel() ──► CANCELLED
                                        ╱   │   ╲
                      exit == 0        ╱    │    ╲  RSS > mem / wall > time / exit != 0
                                      ▼     │     ▼
                                COMPLETED   │   FAILED / OUT_OF_MEMORY / TIMEOUT
                                            │                │
                                            └────────────────┴──► retry(chunks) ──► PENDING

Job-level aggregate state is derived deterministically from chunk states: - Any RUNNING → RUNNING - Else any PENDING → PENDING - Else all COMPLETED → COMPLETED - Else all CANCELLED → CANCELLED - Else some COMPLETED and some failed/OOM/timeout/cancelled → PARTIAL_FAILURE - Else → FAILED

4.3 MockSlurmBackend vs SlurmSshBackend

  • MockSlurmBackend: Runs real isolated background R worker processes via callr::r_bg() executing the exact same worker.R script and disk checkpoint layout as real SLURM, throttled by max_workers concurrent slots. Continuously polls OS RSS via ps, enforces simulated memory (OUT_OF_MEMORY) and walltime (TIMEOUT) limits, supports deterministic per-chunk fault injection (fail_chunks, oom_chunks, timeout_chunks, fail_once), and cleans up child processes on cancel() and object finalization.
  • SlurmSshBackend: Executes ssh and scp commands via processx::run (or an injectable command_runner callback for deterministic offline contract testing). Uses BatchMode=yes, strict shell quoting, --parsable sbatch submission, combined squeue + sacct status reconciliation (normalizing .batch/.extern job steps and K/M/G/T MaxRSS values), range-compressed surgical retry (--array=2-4,7), and scp artifact retrieval.

5. Non-Blocking Shiny Async Architecture

Shiny runs a single-threaded R event loop per session. Running long statistical workloads synchronously inside an observeEvent() freezes all UI controls, tabs, and WebSocket heartbeats.

slurmpilot keeps the Shiny session 100% responsive by delegating all compute to background OS processes (via callr::r_bg for micro-piloting and SlurmBackend for cluster execution) and driving UI updates through lightweight non-blocking polling:

  Browser UI (bslib cards, value boxes, controls)
       ▲  WebSocket updates (non-blocking)          │ user events (pilot/submit/retry/cancel)
       │                                            ▼
  mod_hpc_monitor_server                    mod_hpc_submit_server
   ├── reactiveTimer(poll_ms)                ├── launches pilot via callr::r_bg()
   │    └── calls slurm_status(job)          ├── polls pilot process non-blockingly
   ├── renders KPIs, multi-segment bar,      ├── computes estimate_resources()
   │   chunk table, and log viewer           └── calls slurm_submit() ──► returns job reactive
   └── handles retry / cancel / collect

Key design invariants: 1. Zero blocking calls in reactive observers: Both pilot_run in mod_hpc_submit_server and worker chunks in MockSlurmBackend execute in separate OS processes. 2. Self-throttling polling: reactiveTimer(poll_ms) only triggers backend queries when polling is unpaused and a job is in a non-terminal state (PENDING or RUNNING), automatically going idle on terminal completion and resuming cleanly on retry(). 3. Decoupled module interface: mod_hpc_submit_server() returns reactive getters (job, pilot, resources, is_piloting) which plug directly into mod_hpc_monitor_server(id, job = submit$job). Both modules accept any SlurmBackend (MockSlurmBackend locally or SlurmSshBackend in production) with zero UI code changes.
